slides.title: In One Sentence
slides.big: Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
slides.body: A bond pays a fixed interest amount, so a lower price means a higher yield for the new buyer.

slides.title: How It Works
items: Example: you hold a bond paying 3%.
New bonds now pay 4%, so yours looks weaker.
Buyers pay less for yours, so its price drops.
slides.footer: Hypothetical example, not real market data.
slides.disclaimer: For informational purposes only. Not investment advice.

slides.title: Why It Matters to You
slides.body: Yields shape mortgage rates, savings rates and the value of bond funds in retirement accounts.

slides.title: Remember This
items: Yields up means existing bond prices down.
Yields down means existing bond prices up.
